Rashi on Temurah 7b:10:1.hebrew: אפיק חדא מינייהו - או כולו או מקצתו, ועייל קבלת הדם, דנפקא מלא תקריבו דמיד בן נכר:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:10:1.english: Remove one of them - Either [burning] all of it or [burning] part of it, and insert the collection of the blood, which is derived from "You shall not offer" in [the verse]: "From the hand of a foreigner" [Leviticus 22:25].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:10:2.english: And [the Gemara] objects: [With regard to] collection of the blood, the first tanna does not hold of [it] - And [yet] he counts five [prohibitions].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:11:1.hebrew: רישא רבנן - כלומר, רישא רבנן היא, דלא מחייבי אקבלת הדם, ואפילו הכי קא חשיב ה', וקשיא לאביי:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:11:1.english: The first clause [is according to] the Rabbis - That is to say, the first clause is [according to] the Rabbis, who do not hold [one] liable for the collection of the blood, and even so it counts five [prohibitions]; and [this is] difficult for Abaye.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:1.hebrew: הכהנים ממירים בשלהן - קרבנות שהפריש הכהן לעצמו, אם המיר בהן, נתפסים בתמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:1.english: The priests substitute for their own [offerings] - Sacrifices that the priest designated for himself — if he substituted [another animal] for them, [the substituted animals] take on the status of a substitute.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:2.hebrew: לא בחטאת ואשם - שנתן לו ישראל שיקריבנו לו — אם המיר בו הכהן, אינו עושה תמורה על ידו, דהא אין לו חלק בו אלא משעת הקטרת אימורין ואילך, וזכה בבשר. ואמר בברייתא בהאי פירקא: אין אדם מתפיס בדבר שאינו שלו:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:2.english: Neither for a sin offering nor a guilt offering - That an Israelite gave him to sacrifice for him — if the priest substituted [another animal] for it, it does not effect a substitution through him, for he has no share in it except from the time of the burning of the sacrificial portions onward, and [only then] does he acquire [the right to] the meat. And it is stated in a baraita in this chapter: “A person cannot designate [as a substitute] an item that is not his.”

Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:3.hebrew: ולא בבכור - שנתן לו ישראל, וטעמא מפרש הכא במשנה גופה:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:3.english: Nor for a firstborn - That an Israelite gave to him, and the reason is explained here in the mishna itself.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:4.hebrew: מפני מה אין - הכהנים ממירין בבכור? והלא כולו שלהן הוא, ומחיים הוא נותנו לו, ואין הישראל מתכפר בו:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:4.english: For what reason do [they] not - [Why do] the priests not substitute for a firstborn? For is it not entirely theirs, and [the Israelite] gives it to him while [it is still] alive, and the Israelite does not achieve atonement through it?

Rashi on Temurah 7b:12:5.english: Just as the priests do not substitute for a sin offering and a guilt offering - For this is certainly obvious to us, that [the priest] does not acquire them except from the burning of the sacrificial portions onward.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:13:1.hebrew: מה לי אינו ממיר בחטאת ואשם - כלומר, דין הוא שאין כהנים ממירין בחטאת ואשם, כו':
Rashi on Temurah 7b:13:1.english: What is it to me [if] he does not substitute for a sin offering and a guilt offering - That is to say: It stands to reason that priests do not substitute for a sin offering and a guilt offering, etc.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:13:2.hebrew: הוא ותמורתו - מקיש התמורה להקדש עצמו: היכן קדושה חלה על ההקדש? בבית הבעלים. אף תמורה לא תחול אלא בבית הבעלים, אבל בבית כהן לא חיילא לגמרי. הלכך, אין כהן ממיר בבכור; אבל ישראל, אם המיר בו, נתפס בקדושה, שהרי ברשותו חלה קדושה על הבכור:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:13:2.english: It and its substitute - [The verse] juxtaposes the substitute to the consecrated animal itself: Where does sanctity take effect upon the consecrated animal? In the house of the owner. So too, substitution takes effect only in the house of the owner, but in the house of a priest it does not take effect at all. Therefore, a priest cannot substitute for a firstborn; but an Israelite, if he substituted for it, [the substitute] becomes imbued with sanctity, as it was in his possession that sanctity took effect upon the firstborn.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:1.hebrew: מוכרין אותו תמים חי - השתא משמע בין בזמן המקדש בין בזמן הזה, והכי משמע: אם בית המקדש קיים, מוכרין אותו כהן לכהן חי, ואותו כהן יקריבנו. אבל שחוט — לא, דבזיון קדשים הוא, דלאו אורח ארעא לעשות סחורה בדבר שקרב ממנו למזבח. ואי בזמן הזה הוא, מוכרין אותו תמים חי — בין כהן לכהן, בין כהן לישראל — והלוקח ימתין עד שיפול בו מום ויאכלנו, דבכור בזמן הזה, משנפל בו מום, אין בו אלא איסור גזל שגזל את הכהן, ואם מכרו כהן או נתנו לו, מותר לאוכלו. וכדאמרינן בבכורות [בפ' כל פסולי המוקדשין] (דף לב:) גבי בכור בעל מום (כל פסולי המוקדשין): ב"ה מתירין, ואפי' עובד כוכבים מותר לאכול הימנו. אבל בתם שחוט בזמן הזה — ליכא:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:1.english: One may sell it unblemished [while] alive - Now [at this point in the Gemara, before Rav Naḥman qualifies the mishna, it] implies [that this applies] both in the time of the Temple and in the present time, and this is what it means: If the Temple is standing, a priest may sell it alive to [another] priest, and that priest will sacrifice it. However, [when it is] slaughtered, [he may] not [sell it], as it is a degradation of consecrated items, for it is not proper conduct to conduct commerce with something from which [parts] are sacrificed on the Altar. And if it is in the present time, one may sell it unblemished [while] alive — whether [from] a priest to a priest or [from] a priest to an Israelite — and the buyer will wait until a blemish befalls it and [then] eat it, for regarding a firstborn in the present time, once a blemish has befallen it, it entails only the prohibition of robbery in that he robbed the priest; and if a priest sold it or gave it to him, it is permitted to eat it. And as we say in Bekhorot [in the chapter Kol P’sulei HaMukdashin] (32b) regarding a blemished firstborn (all disqualified consecrated animals): Beit Hillel permit [it], and even an idolater is permitted to eat from it. However, regarding an unblemished [firstborn] slaughtered in the present time, there is no [such case].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:2.hebrew: ומקדש בו - כהן את האשה, דממוניה הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:2.english: And [one] betroths with it - A priest [betroths] a woman, for it is his property.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:3.english: They taught [this] only - That a priest can sell it alive.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:4.english: Only in the present time - For it does not stand for sacrifice.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:5.hebrew: ואית לכהן זכייה בגויה - מחיים, דבזמן הזה נמי הוו הבכורות לכהנים:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:5.english: And the priest has a right of acquisition in it - While [it is] alive; for in the present time as well, firstborn [animals] belong to the priests.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:14:6.english: One may not sell it unblemished [while] alive - For the priest has no [right of] acquisition in it except from the burning of the sacrificial portions onward.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:15:1.english: Is there an unblemished, slaughtered [firstborn] - For that would be [slaughtering] consecrated animals outside [the Temple].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:16:1.hebrew: מי קתני שחוט לא - דמשמע מינה דלאו בזמן הזה, דבזמן הזה ליכא תם שחוט:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:16:1.english: Does it teach: [Once] slaughtered, no? - So that one would infer from it that [the mishna is] not [speaking of] the present, since in the present there is no unblemished slaughtered [firstborn].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:16:2.hebrew: הא גופא קמ"ל - כלומר, מאי דקתני בברייתא — גופה איצטריך לאשמועינן דמוכרין אותו תמים חי, דס"ד דלית בהו זכייה עד שיפול בו מום; ולאו משום דתידוק מינה שחוט לא, דהא בזמן הזה קמיירי, ובזמן הזה ליכא תם שחוט:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:16:2.english: It teaches us this itself - That is to say, that which is taught in the baraita — [the ruling] itself was needed to teach us that one may sell it unblemished [while] alive, for you might have thought that [the priests] have no right of acquisition in them until a blemish falls upon it; and not because you should infer from it [that when] slaughtered, [it may] not [be sold], for it is dealing with the present [era], and in the present [era] there is no slaughtered unblemished [firstborn].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:1.hebrew: נדבה תעשה אותו - לבעל מום, לדמי קדשי בדק הבית — דלמזבח לא אפשר לאקרוביה, דהא כתיב (ויקרא כב): ״לא תתנו מהם וגו'״:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:1.english: You may offer it for a gift - [This refers] to a blemished animal, for the monetary value of [items] consecrated for Temple maintenance, since it is not possible to sacrifice it on the altar, for behold, it is written (Leviticus 22:22): “You shall not make of them [an offering by fire upon the altar to the Lord].”

Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:2.english: I only have [derived] - An inclusion to consecrate a blemished animal for Temple maintenance.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:3.hebrew: אלא - על ידי נדבה, כגון: ״הרי זו לבדק הבית״:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:3.english: Rather - By way of a donation, such as: “This [animal] is for Temple maintenance.”

Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:4.hebrew: נדר מנין - שאם אמר: "הרי עלי בהמה לדמי בדק הבית", שמצוה להפריש בעל מום — תלמוד לומר: "ולנדר". והכי נמי דריש: "נדבה תעשה אותו ולנדר" — כלומר: וכן לנדר:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:1:4.english: From where [is] a vow [derived] - That if one said: “Behold, it is incumbent upon me [to give] an animal for the value of Temple maintenance,” that it is a mitzva to set aside a blemished animal — the verse states: “And for a vow.” And this is also how he expounds [the verse]: “You may make it a gift, and for a vow” — that is to say: and likewise for a vow.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:1.english: “It shall not be accepted” — these are altar offerings - For acceptance applies to them.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:2.hebrew: אין לי אלא נדר - דנדר סמוך ל״לא ירצה״, ומשמע דאם נדר ״הרי עלי עולה״, לא יביא בעלת מום:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:2.english: I have [derived] only a vow - For "vow" is adjacent to "it shall not be accepted," and it implies that if one vowed, "Behold, upon me is a burnt offering," he may not bring a blemished [animal].

Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:3.english: From where [is it derived for] a gift [offering] - That one is not permitted to say regarding a blemished [animal]: “This [animal] is for the altar.”

Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:4.hebrew: תלמוד לומר נדבה - ולנדר לא ירצה, והכי מידריש: נדבה אשר תעשה אותו, או נדר — לא ירצה:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:4.english: The verse states: “A gift” - “And for a vow it shall not be accepted” — and this is how it is expounded: [Whether it is] a gift that you make it, or a vow, it shall not be accepted.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:5.hebrew: רבי אמר לא ירצה בהרצאת גופו הכתוב מדבר - שלא יקריבנו, והיינו נמי קדשי מזבח כתנא קמא:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:2:5.english: Rabbi said: “It shall not be accepted” — the verse is speaking of the acceptance of its body - That one may not sacrifice it; and this is also altar offerings, like the first tanna.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:1.hebrew: וקבעי אלא אותו למאי אתא - כלומר, תינח כוליה קרא מוקמת לדרשא, דקא דרשת האי נדבה ונדר:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:1.english: And [the Gemara] asks: But what did “it” come [to teach]? - That is to say: Granted, you establish the entire verse for an exposition, as you expounded this “gift” and “vow”.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:2.hebrew: אלא אותו - דכתיב (שם) נדבה תעשה אותו, למה לי:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:2.english: Rather, "it" - That which is written (ibid.), "You may make it a freewill offering" — why do I need [it]?

Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:3.english: It - A blemished [animal] you may consecrate for Temple maintenance, etc.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:4.hebrew: עובר בעשה - אהאי עשה דאמרינן ״ואי אתה מקדיש תמימים״, דהיינו לאו הבא מכלל עשה, ועשה הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:4:4.english: Transgresses a positive mitzva - [He transgresses] this positive mitzva that we stated: “And you may not consecrate unblemished [animals],” which is a prohibition derived from a positive mitzva, and it is [considered] a positive mitzva.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:6:1.english: It was not stated in Deuteronomy - That is to say, in that passage.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:6:2.hebrew: לא אמור - כלומר, הכי אמר הקב"ה: לאו אמור להם לישראל, דלאו איכא הכא — דאי עברי אהך פרשה, עוברין בלאו:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:6:2.english: “No, say” - That is to say, thus said the Holy One, Blessed be He: “Say a prohibition to them, to Israel,” for there is a prohibition here, so that if they transgress this passage, they violate a negative commandment.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:7:1.english: The limbs, etc. - The pieces [cut] according to the law of a burnt offering.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:7:2.hebrew: על לאו שבכללות - דהקטרת כולו ומקצתו מחד לאו נפקי — ואשה לא תתנו מהם — כדפרישית לעיל. אבל לכולהו איכא לאו לכל חד וחד: דהקדש נפיק מכל אשר בו מום לא תקריבו, ודרשינן ליה לעיל (תמורה דף ו:) לא תקדישו; ושחיטה — מלא תקריבו אלה לה', דגבי עורת או שבור; וזריקה — מלא תקריבו, דגבי מעוך וכתות (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ב). והאי אין לוקין דאמר אביי — אין לוקין תרתי קאמר, אבל חדא איכא, ואליבא למאן דאמר חדא מיהא לקי אלאו שבכללות בשילהי פרק שני דפסחים (מא:):
Rashi on Temurah 7b:7:2.english: For a general prohibition - For the burning of all of it and [the burning of] part of it are derived from a single negative prohibition — "and an offering made by fire you shall not put of them" [Leviticus 22:22] — as I explained above. But for all the others, there is a [distinct] negative prohibition for each and every one: for [the prohibition of] consecration is derived from "Whatever has a blemish, you shall not offer" [Leviticus 22:20], and we interpreted it above (Temurah 6b): "You shall not consecrate"; and [the prohibition of] slaughter is from "you shall not offer these unto the LORD" [Leviticus 22:22], which is [stated] in reference to "blind, or broken"; and [the prohibition of] sprinkling [the blood] is from "you shall not offer" [Leviticus 22:24], which is [stated] in reference to "bruised, or crushed" (Leviticus 22:22). And this [statement], "One is not flogged," that Abaye said means: one is not flogged twice, but there is one [set of lashes]; and [this is] in accordance with the one who says that one receives at least one [set of lashes] for a general prohibition, at the end of the second chapter of Pesachim (41b).

Rashi on Temurah 7b:8:1.english: On account of five categories - And [the baraita] counts these two [prohibitions] as two.

Rashi on Temurah 7b:9:1.hebrew: בגברי קתני - דלאו בהכי עסקינן, דאי עבדינהו לתרוייהו לילקי תרי; אלא מילי מילי קתני: שאם הקטיר כולו — עובר משום ״בל תקטירו כולו״, או אם אדם אחד מקטיר מקצתו — לוקה משום מקצתו; אבל אי מקטיר חד לכולהו — לא לקי אלא משום כולו:
Rashi on Temurah 7b:9:1.english: [The baraita] teaches with regard to [different] men - For we are not dealing with [a case where], if he did both of them, he would be flogged twice; rather, it teaches individual cases: that if [one] burned all of it, he violates [the prohibition] on account of “You shall not burn all of it,” or if one person burns part of it, he is flogged on account of [burning] part of it; but if one [person] burns both of them, he is flogged only on account of [burning] all of it.

Tosafot on Temurah 7b:13:1.hebrew: שאין זכין בחייהן - ואם תאמר: ואי זכין בהן בחייהן, היכי מימר למאן דאמר בגמרא "בתר מתכפר אזלינן"? ויש לומר: דר"ל "אף בתר מתכפר", ולאו לאפוקי בעלים אתי:
Tosafot on Temurah 7b:13:1.english: "Which they do not acquire during their lifetimes" - And if you say: And [even] if they do acquire [rights in] them during their lifetimes, how could [a priest] substitute, according to the one who says in the Gemara [that] we follow the one who achieves atonement? And one can say: That he meant [to say], "We also follow the one who achieves atonement," and it did not come to exclude the owner.

Tosafot on Temurah 7b:14:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא בזמן הזה - וא"ת: האמר פרק שור שנגח הפרה (ב"ק דף נג:), שור ושור פסולי המוקדשין שנגחו — אביי אמר: חצי נזק, ומוקי לה במועד; אבל שור של פסולי המוקדשין פטור, אלמא לאו "רעהו" קרינא ביה! וקאמר התם נמי, דשור של הדיוט שנגח שור של פסולי המוקדשין חייב — אלמא משמע דקרינא ביה "רעהו". וצריך לומר, דקמייתא מיירי בבכור דלא מצי פריק, וברייתא בשאר קדשים דפריק להו במומן. והתם בזמן הזה איירי, שהרי האמוראים דאיירי התם עלה לא הוו בזמן הבית, ואפילו הכי קאמר התם דלאו ממונו הוא; ואם כן קשה, דהכא אמר דממונו הוא בזמן הזה! וצריך לומר, דהכא אתייא כרבי יוסי הגלילי וההיא דהתם כרבנן. ואע"ג דבפ' קמא דב"ק (דף יב: ושם ד"ה ואם) אמר: "[ולשני] הא כרבי יוסי [והא כרבנן]" — צ"ל דלפי זה לא מיתוקמא ההיא סוגיא דפרק הפרה:
Tosafot on Temurah 7b:14:1.english: "They taught only with regard to the present" - And if you say: Didn't [the Gemara] say in the chapter [entitled] "Shor Shenagach HaParah" (Bava Kamma 53b): With regard to an ox [of an ordinary person] and an ox of disqualified consecrated animals that [jointly] gored [another ox], Abaye said: [The owner of the ordinary ox pays] half-damages; and [the Gemara] establishes it [as dealing] with a forewarned [ox] (mu'ad), but the ox of disqualified consecrated animals is exempt — evidently, we do not read concerning it "[the ox of] his neighbor"; and it also says there that [in the case of] an ox belonging to an ordinary person that gored an ox of disqualified consecrated animals, [the owner] is liable — evidently implying that we do read concerning it "[the ox of] his neighbor"; and one must say that the former [case] is dealing with a firstborn [offering] (bekhor), which cannot be redeemed, and the baraita [is dealing] with other consecrated animals, which were redeemed upon their blemish; and there [in the case of the firstborn], it is dealing with the present [post-Temple] time, for the Amora'im who discussed it there were not [alive] during the Temple era, and even so, it says there that it is not his monetary property; and if so, this is difficult, as here [in our sugya] it said that it is his monetary property in the present time! And one must say that here [our sugya] follows Rabbi Yose HaGelili, and that [sugya] there follows the Rabbis. And even though in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (12b, and there s.v. Ve'im) it said: "[And let him answer:] this is according to Rabbi Yose [and that is according to the Rabbis]" — one must say that according to this, that sugya of Perek HaParah cannot be established [as unanimous, but only according to the Rabbis].

Tosafot on Temurah 7b:7:1.hebrew: אביי אמר אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות - פרש"י: דהא "אין לוקין" דאמר אביי — "אין לוקין תרתי" קאמר, אבל חדא לקי, ואליבא דמ"ד חדא מיהא לקי אלאו שבכללות בשילהי פ' כל שעה (פסחים דף מא:). לשון רש"י. וכן מוכח הסוגיא:
Tosafot on Temurah 7b:7:1.english: "Abaye said: One is not flogged for a general prohibition" - Rashi explains that this "one is not flogged" that Abaye stated means "one is not flogged twice," but one is flogged once, and [this is] in accordance with the one who holds [that] one is at least flogged once for a general prohibition at the end of the chapter "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 41b). [This is] the wording of Rashi. And so the sugya proves.
